findings.title: Content-Security-Policy is not set, and the site has signed-in users
findings.evidence:
Response headers for https://priceoye.pk/ contain no `content-security-policy`.
The site has a login form or session cookie, which is what raises this above hygiene.
findings.impact: There is no second line of defence if a cross-site scripting bug is ever introduced: any injected script runs with full access to the page.
findings.fix: Start with a report-only policy to find what the site actually loads, then enforce a policy that names the script sources you trust.

findings.title: 2 standard security header(s) are not set
findings.evidence:
Content-Security-Policy: not present
Referrer-Policy: not present

Present: HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors
findings.impact: These headers are the browser-side defences a site opts into. Individually none of them is a vulnerability; together their absence means a bug elsewhere has nothing standing in its way.
findings.fix: Set them once at the edge or in middleware so every response carries them: Start with a report-only policy to find what the site actually loads, then enforce a policy that names the script sources you trust. Send `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.

positives: The site is served over HTTPS.
Plain HTTP correctly redirects to HTTPS.
The HTTPS certificate is valid for another 30 days.
No credentials were found in the JavaScript served to visitors.
Session cookies are set HttpOnly and Secure.
